Article Title: Former AAP spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joins Congress
Article Text:
Priyanka Kakkar joined the Congress. (IANS)

NEW DELHI: Former Aam Aadmi Party(AAP) spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joined the Congress on Saturday, saying she could no longer defend the “indefensible”.After joining Congress, Kakkar praised Rahul Gandhi , calling him a resilient leader and saying she had seen how he and the party continued to withstand attacks against them.“If there is one leader who is not afraid to promote his ideas, it is Rahul Gandhi. I observed that he is the only leader who has not shed tears for the cameras. He is the only leader today who has not done that. He is resilient. I have seen how he was humiliated and how an entire machinery was deployed to put him down. But Rahul Gandhi and the Congress remained resilient,” Kakkar said.“Their authenticity is their soul. I saw that there is a soul in this party as well, which I found missing in other parties. And I say this from lived experience,” she added.Explaining her decision to leave AAP, Kakkar referred to what she described as a shift in the party's functioning and leadership.“There was a time when it was said that AAP would not take a bungalow or a car. But later, choppers started being used for private travel, and I could no longer defend the indefensible,” she said.“I drew a line when I saw that the Aam Aadmi Party, which at one point had attracted people with great substance and intelligence, was unable to retain them,” Kakkar added.She also criticised the appointment of people to senior positions in Punjab, saying, “Who are the people being brought in now? New people who have not even worked at the booth level are being brought from Rajasthan and given senior positions in Punjab, along with bungalows and cars.”“How long can I defend the indefensible?” she added.Kakkar also backed Rahul Gandhi's ongoing criticism of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the electoral-roll revision and his allegations concerning voter rights. Gandhi has been demanding Kumar's resignation and has accused the Election Commission of irregularities in the electoral process.“I also saw how Rahul Gandhi has continuously launched a campaign against traitor Gyanesh Kumar. He has made everyone, including us, aware of this issue,” Kakkar said.“We have to make the public aware of how, according to him, our only voting right is being stolen by Gyanesh Kumar and put into PM Modi's account. This has to stop.”“Therefore, we must all come together now to support the Congress and support Rahul Gandhi in his authentic fight to keep the idea of India alive,” she added.
Article Summary: Former aam aadmi party spokesperson priyanka kakkar joined the congress on saturday. Kakkar praised rahul gandhi, calling him a resilient leader and saying she had seen how he and the party continued to withstand attacks against them. She also backed rahul gandhi's ongoing criticism of chief election commissioner gyanesh kumar over the electoral-roll revision.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi launches 'Satyagraha' website for information on current protests across India
Article Text:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Congress MP and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday launched “ Satyagraha ," a digital platform aimed at consolidating information on various issue-based protests taking place across the country.The website was launched a day after the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi , whose philosophy of “Satyagraha” — peaceful resistance for truth — Rahul Gandhi invoked.In a post on X, the Raebareli MP noted that protesters can submit details about their causes, find similar movements across the country through an interactive map and seek direct support.“People across the country are fighting for their rights and often fighting alone. Gen Z, students, farmers, tribals, Dalits, women — every struggle has its own story. But the voice that rises alone often gets suppressed. ‘Satyagraha’ is an initiative to bring these voices together on a map. Bapu taught us this; truth is the greatest weapon. But an even greater weapon is standing together with truth in unity. If you’re also fighting against any injustice, share your story. It will take two minutes,” Rahul Gandhi said.“Your story will appear on the map. You’ll see who else is fighting like you. And I’ll do whatever I can, in Parliament, on the streets, by writing letters, standing with you wherever I’m needed, as the Leader of the Opposition; this is my responsibility,” the former Congress president added.In a video accompanying the post, Rahul Gandhi asserted that as the leader of opposition, it was his “responsibility” to consolidate information about protests across the country in one place.“Protests are taking place in every corner of the country. Someone is speaking about students, someone is speaking about women, someone is protesting against price rise, so there are lakhs of different protests happening across the country. I am the Leader of Opposition, and I wanted us to consolidate the information about all these protests in one place. That is why we have launched the Satyagraha website for you. Whatever your protest may be, big or small, enter your name, the name of your group, and detail what the protest is about. And if we can help you, or if you seek help from us, we will gladly support you,” Rahul Gandhi said.
Article Summary: Congress leader rahul gandhi launches a digital platform aimed at consolidating information on various issue-based protests taking place across the country. The website was launched a day after the 157th birth anniversary of mahatma gandhi, whose philosophy of ‘satyagraha’ — peaceful resistance for truth — rahul gandhi invoked.

Article Title: Pacific to pacify ties? Washington sends US admiral to India as relations face strain
Article Text:
Samuel Paparo's visit comes after a run of statements in Washington.

Press release by the US Embassy in India.

What Washington has put on record

The China question in the background

NEW DELHI: American admiral Samuel J. Paparo, who leads US Indo-Pacific Command, is in India from 3 to 8 October. It is his second visit this year.The US Embassy said the trip is meant to push forward the "major defense partnership" and deepen cooperation between the two militaries.Its list of topics includes digital transformation, emerging technologies and regional strategic stability. It also names "defense energy resilience" and an "increasingly competitive technology landscape", though it does not spell out what either would involve.On his earlier trip, Paparo visited Delhi, Chandimandir and Bengaluru. He met the Chief of Defence Staff and the Navy chief, and discussed security along India's western and northern borders.Last month, Paparo conducted a series of key bilateral and multilateral meetings on the sidelines of the 28th Indo-Pacific Chiefs of defence conference in Victoria, Canada, held from August 31 to September 2.According to the US Pacific Command (US PACOM), Paparo highlighted "the importance of strong bilateral and multilateral relationships in advancing regional security and deterrence".Throughout the conference, the US commander engaged in discussions with the Defence Cooperation Council and the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad), and joined military leadership from Asean nations.Paparo also connected with defence counterparts from Australia and the United Kingdom for an Aukus dialogue, and conferred with Adm. Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, chair of the Nato Military Committee.US Pacific Command noted that Paparo carried out bilateral discussions focused on "strengthening operational cooperation, information-sharing, maritime security and readiness across the Indo-Pacific" with senior representatives from numerous partner nations.The participating countries included Bangladesh, Brunei, Cambodia, Canada, France, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Mongolia, New Zealand, the Republic of Korea, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam.Paparo's visit comes after a run of statements in Washington. An update on how the 2026 National Defense Strategy is being carried out, sent to the Senate Armed Services Committee, places India under the heading of burden-sharing, the idea that allies and partners should take on more of the load."Finally, and crucially given its regional standing and power, we are also building on our strong defence relationship with India, with the recent signature of a 10-year bilateral defence framework and a separate framework to strengthen undersea cooperation," the update said.Testifying before lawmakers in April, Paparo said the relationship with India had seen "transformative growth through increasingly complex military exercises, defence sales, and strategic dialogue".However, the recent Trump tariffs and the punitive measures against India for buying Russian oil, and a stuck trade deal has undoubetly strained the ties between both nations.Paparo had also pointed to cooperation on maritime security and underwater awareness, including India's planned purchase of MQ-9B drones through US foreign military sales. He also described India as one of the partners he visits and coordinates with most often.He said India "continues to be a source of stability within South Asia", and cited its investments in Sri Lanka and its agreements with Mauritius, which he said help keep strategic infrastructure "free of adversarial influences". On Pakistan, he noted that recent military exchanges had extended beyond traditionally disputed areas, but said India's main focus remained "maintaining deterrence and credible warfighting capability within the region writ large. "None of this is discussed in isolation from China as Paparo himself has said Beijing's actions, along with its deepening ties to Russia and North Korea, make for a complex challenge to regional stability. He calls alliances and partnerships Washington's "greatest asymmetric advantage", and the Quad, which brings together the US, India, Japan and Australia, is part of that picture. Though Quad his been pushed to a back burner under the Tump 2.0.At a regional security conference in Malaysia, Paparo said some actors were using "false claims of legitimacy" to justify coercion. "That's not the rule of law. That's the rule by law. That distinction between law as a tool of order versus law as a weapon of raw power, is the defining fault line of our time," he said. He added that the US was deterring China "through strength, not through confrontation".In the South China Sea, Manila has accused Beijing of dangerous manoeuvres, water cannon attacks and attempts to block resupply missions around a disputed shoal. China denies this. Philippine defence secretary Gilberto Teodoro said, "China is everywhere … this is a matter of concern," and pointed to a recent Chinese ballistic missile launch into the Pacific.At the congressional hearing, Representative Adam Smith said partners needed reassurance. "We need to maintain those relationships. We need to let those folks know that we are there and they can depend on us," he said.
Article Summary: American admiral samuel j. paparo, who leads us indo-pacific command, is in india from 3 to 8 october. It is his second visit this year. Us embassy said the trip is meant to push forward the "major defense partnership" and deepen cooperation between the two militaries.

Article Title: Flydubai attack: Co-pilot identified as Hamam Alhamami was barred from flying in Oman over 'extremist views'
Article Text:
As per reports, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. His alleged views are being examined as part of a wider investigation into possible Islamic radicalisation and terrorist motives

Removed from Oman Air training role

Pro-Palestinian material found among belongings

Questions over clearance for Tel Aviv flight

Who is Hamam Alhamami?

What happened aboard flydubai flight

The Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv has been identified as Hamam Alhamami. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views.Al Arabiya English, citing sources, reported that he had spent much of his time outside Oman, particularly in Syria, where he was allegedly influenced by extremist ideas before travelling to the UAE.The revelations follow a CNN report that Alhamami had been removed from a training role at Oman Air, Oman's national carrier, last year. However, he was later given another role at the airline, the report said, citing a regional diplomatic source familiar with the matter.Further reports have raised questions about Alhamami's alleged ideological views. i24 News, citing an Emirati source, reported that leaflets and publications from “Free Palestine” groups, along with other pro-Palestinian material, were found among his belongings.According to the report, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. The report said investigators were examining the material as part of a broader probe into his alleged Islamic radicalisation and possible terrorist motives.The reports have also raised questions about how Alhamami was cleared to serve on a Tel Aviv-bound flight despite being an Omani citizen. Oman does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations with the country.An Israeli official told CNN that several agencies, including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the Transportation Ministry, were investigating how Alhamami came to be part of the flight crew.According to the report, Alhamami is an Omani citizen. He was born in the United Arab Emirates to an Omani father and Syrian mother and spent several years of his life in the UAE. The Jerusalem Post, citing sources close to the investigation, reported that he did not hold a second nationality.CNN reported that Alhamami had worked for flydubai for only eight months. He had previously worked for Royal Air Maroc, Morocco's national carrier.Alhamami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to the UAE after the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk. He is facing a terrorism investigation in the UAE.The September 30 incident took place aboard a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Alhamami allegedly attacked Captain Machchhar inside the cockpit in what is being investigated as a possible terror-driven attempt to bring down the aircraft.The confrontation triggered a steep descent, with the aircraft dropping approximately 16,000 feet within two minutes before a hijacking distress signal was transmitted.Despite suffering severe injuries, Captain Machchhar resisted the attack and managed to open the cockpit door. Flight crew members and passengers then entered the cockpit and restrained Alhamami, allowing the crew to regain control of the aircraft.Two non-duty aviators who were travelling aboard the flight also helped assume control of the aircraft. The plane subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, with all 180 occupants disembarking safely.
Article Summary: Hamam alhamami is the omani co-pilot accused of attacking captain smit machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to tel aviv. He was barred from flying in oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views. Pro-palestinian material was found among his belongings, according to reports.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday said that he had a "productive conversation" with US President Donald Trump and reviewed bilateral cooperation between New Delhi and Washington in various sectors.In a social media post on X, PM Modi said the leaders agreed to maintain close engagement to take their Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward."Had a productive conversation with President Trump. We reviewed our bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas. We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward," PM Modi said."We also exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security," he added.The two leaders agreed to remain in touch as both sides continue to deepen the strategic partnership.This comes days after Trump signed into law a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russia and Iran and giving his administration expanded powers to penalise countries that continue buying Russian oil and gas, including India.The legislation is particularly significant for India because it gives Trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on imports from the five largest buyers of Russian oil or natural gas.India and China are among the major purchasers of Russian crude.Earlier in September, the ministry of external affairs warned the US of the legislation's potential impact on the US-India relationship."This issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side," the ministry had said.
Article Summary: Prime minister narendra modi says he had a "productive conversation" with us president donald trump. The two leaders agreed to maintain close engagement to take their comprehensive global strategic partnership forward. This comes days after trump signed into law a sweeping sanctions package targeting russia and iran.

Article Title: Warring out, Pargat Singh in: Has Congress solved Punjab crisis or created more confusion?
Article Text:
Amrinder Raja Warring, Pargat SIngh

Warring is out, but not down

Amarinder Singh Raja Warring hints that Sachin Pilot may have played a role in his exit.

Amarinder Singh Raja Warring said he stepped down as Punjab Congress chief after reading the 'direction of the wind'

How the Channi-Warring tussle began

Warring out, but Channi not in

2022 rerun in Punjab

NEW DELHI: The churn in Punjab Congress is now complete. Or is it?Amarinder Singh Raja Warring is out and Pargat Singh is the new Punjab Congress president. The change came hours after Warring resigned from the post, ending his more than four-year stint as state party chief. Warring met Rahul Gandhi on Friday and formally submitted his resignation. A day earlier, he had changed his X bio to “Former PPCC President”, signalling the leadership change."He (Rahul Gandhi) gave me a lot of love. He sought information about the current political situation in Punjab, on what is happening with the government and what we should be doing there," Warring said after his meeting.Hours later, the Congress announced the appointment of Pargat Singh as the new Punjab Congress president with immediate effect. The party also appreciated the contribution of outgoing president Warring.The change in Punjab Congress comes after months of infighting over who should lead the Congress into the 2027 assembly election. The crisis was triggered by Congress’s decision to retain Warring as state unit president in July, ignoring the claims of former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi . So, Warring’s exit marks a victory for Channi and his supporters, but the entry of Pargat Singh means he does not gain from Warring's loss.Warring may be out of his post, but has dropped strong hints that his fight may be far from over. Hours after formally stepping down, Warring targeted his detractors, signalling he is not leaving the field yet. If Warring’s remarks against party incharge Sachin Pilot are an indication to go by, we could well see a reversal of roles in Punjab Congress infighting.In an interaction with news agency ANI, Warring said, “I feel that Sachin Pilot must have decided it was time to remove ‘Raja’ from the post.” Warring, though, added that he had “no concrete proof” of this.Warring added he had not spoken to Pilot about his exit, but had heard that the state Congress incharge may have recommended a change. “Perhaps the in-charge mentioned that Raja Warring would have to be replaced,” he said when asked about the reasons for his resignation.Taking digs at those responsible for his exit, Warring said nobody had formally asked him to resign. Instead, he had simply read the “direction of the wind”."Just like elder women who could tell by reading the direction of the wind whether it was going to rain... I observed the situation closely, and it never reached the point where someone had to ask me to resign," Warring told IANS.That, he said, was why he changed his X bio to “Former PPCC President” even before formally submitting his resignation to Rahul Gandhi.The timing and the turn of events are hard to miss. Nearly a month ago, Congress removed former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel as Punjab in-charge after the Channi faction openly rebelled against him. Baghel was accused of favouring Warring and was eventually replaced by Sachin Pilot.But now, Warring appears ready to open a front against Pilot and, of course, also Channi.That also raises questions about whether replacing Baghel with Pilot has actually helped Congress settle the Punjab crisis. Sugata Srinivasaraju, senior political analyst and author, believes that the leadership change appears to have created more confusion rather than resolving the crisis at hand."What is it that the Congress saw in Pilot that they did not see in Baghel? If you thought Baghel was part of the problem, now Pilot has also become part of the problem. He’s not part of the solution," he said.According to him, Congress may now have ended up with an even bigger problem. "All of them were against Warring. Now Warring goes out and Channi has not been catered to. So we don't know what's going to happen."Both Baghel and Warring are now out of their roles in Punjab Congress. For the Channi camp, it means one of their biggest demands has been met. But with Pargat Singh in the chair, will today's change end weeks of internal feud and bickering in Punjab Congress? Perhaps not.To understand why Warring’s exit and Pargat's entry may not be the end of the crisis, it helps to go back to where the tussle began.The crisis began on July 1, when the Congress leadership announced that Warring would continue as Punjab Congress president and Channi would head the campaign committee. Senior leaders Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa and Vijay Inder Singla were also given specific roles for the 2027 assembly election.On paper, it looked like an attempt to balance competing camps. In practice, it did the opposite.Channi’s supporters questioned why Warring was being retained as state chief and began pushing for a larger role for the former chief minister. What was meant to settle the leadership question instead reopened old faultlines within the party.Warring had been appointed Punjab Congress president after the party’s crushing defeat to AAP in the 2022 assembly election. Channi had been the party’s chief ministerial face in that campaign but lost both seats he contested.Warring was then brought in by the Congress high command (read Rahul Gandhi) to rebuild the organisation and prepare it for the next election. For nearly four years, however, the Congress did not clearly announce who would lead its 2027 campaign.When it finally tried to do that in July, the compromise pleased no one.Bhupesh Baghel, who was then Punjab in-charge, tried to defuse the tussle between the Channi and Warring camps but was also caught in the crossfire and forced out of the state.His replacement, Sachin Pilot, initially managed to bring the rival factions onto the same stage during the Congress protest over the Gulzar Singh suicide case. But that show of unity did not last long.What followed was another round of meetings, complaints and feedback to the high command and, eventually, Warring's exit and Pargat's entry.The Congress high command acted swiftly after Warring's exit and handed over the baton to Pargat Singh. The three-time Congress MLA from Jalandhar Cantt and former Indian hockey captain who has served as Punjab cabinet minister in Charanjit Singh Channi cabinet, has his task cut out.Pargat's name was doing the rounds along with other key contenders which included, former MLA Rana KP Singh, Raja Sansi MLA Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria, former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa. But the frontrunner before today's appointment was former PWD minister and MP Vijay Inder Singla, who was appointed chairperson of the Congress Election Management and Coordination Committee in the July reshuffle."I am a loyal soldier of the party, and at all times, as a worker of the party, whatever responsibility I have been given, I have always fulfilled my duties. And in the coming times as well, we will work together with everyone in the same manner," Singla had said earlier reacting to speculations that he could replace Warring.However that did not happen.And this is where the leadership change in Punjab Congress becomes more interesting.The Channi camp had openly demanded that the former CM should lead the party into the next elections. In fact, their contention all along was that Warring should be replaced by Channi. But today's announcement would leave them disappointed much like the other contenders including Singla.With the Congress picking up Pargat Singh as the compromise candidate, it is a rerun of what happened in the run up to the 2022 elections.And that brings Punjab Congress back to a very familiar problem of bitter power tussle between state leaders. A problem that played a key role in the party’s defeat in 2022.Ahead of the 2022 assembly election, then chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh and Navjot Singh Sidhu were locked in a bitter leadership battle. Sidhu wanted a bigger role in leading the party into the election, while Amarinder resisted attempts to cut into his authority.The Congress leadership allowed the dispute to drag on until the crisis became impossible to contain. Eventually, Amarinder Singh was removed as chief minister. Charanjit Singh Channi emerged as the compromise candidate of Congress high command and was made the chief minister.But the compromise did not end the factional war. Congress went into the election divided and suffered a historic defeat, with AAP sweeping into power.Four years later, the names have changed, but the problem looks strikingly similar.Srinivasaraju sees a larger pattern in Punjab Congress's repeated leadership tussles."Punjab Congress has not been able to resolve it at all. They've had five long years after Amarinder Singh’s exit and they have still not got it right," he said.His argument is that every time Congress begins to see a chance of returning to power in Punjab, competing factions become more active and start weakening the organisation from within."We have seen that with Navjot Singh Sidhu and Amarinder Singh," he said, adding that similar mistakes "seem to be getting repeated".Once again, both the rival leaders - Channi and Warring - are out. But the battle for Channi is still half won. And with Warring all set for a rebel role, the road ahead for the former Punjab chief minister may not be easy.With Warring’s loss not translating into Channi's gain, it will be interesting to see if the Congress's compromise candidate ends this leadership fight once and for all without starting another power tussle?
Article Summary: Amarinder singh raja warring steps down as punjab congress chief. Pargat singh is the new punjab congress president. Warring hints that sachin pilot may have played a role in his exit. Pargat singh has been appointed as the new state chief of punjab congress. Pargat replaces bhupesh baghel, who was forced out of the party in july.

Article Title: The midnight rescue of Karachi's Mahatma Gandhi
Article Text:

G. Parthasarathy has served as India’s Consulate General in Karachi and as India’s High Commissioner in Islamabad.

One of the first things I did when I returned to Pakistan in early 2000, this time as the Indian High Commissioner, was to pay my respects to an imposing bronze statue of Mahatma Gandhi. One of only two Gandhi statutes in Pakistan, Bapuji stands tall at the lobby of the Indian High Commission in Islamabad, famed walking stick in hand, gazing into the distance.The tale of how a pre-Partition statue found its way to its eventual home in the Indian High Commission is a fascinating saga reflecting the tangled tumultuous history of our two countries. It is a journey in which I was honoured to have played a small part.According to several accounts, the statue originally stood outside the Sindh high court on what was known as Kings Way in Karachi. It had been commissioned by the Indian merchant association sometime in the 1930s to commemorate the historic Karachi session of the Indian National Congress. The plaque underneath the life-size monument apparently read: “Mahatma Gandhi – the reputability of freedom, truth and nonviolence.Partition brought the inevitable dislocation. With communal riots engulfing Karachi in 1948, there was fear that the statue would be torn down amidst mob fury. Accounts vary on what exactly happened, but apparently after the intervention of Jamshed Nussranwanji Mehta, a Parsi and former Mayor of Karachi, the statue was surreptiously taken down and moved quietly to the home of the Cowasjees, a leading Parsi family of Karachi.And there it lay for more than thirty years…A few months into my first stint in Pakistan as Consul General in Karachi, a middle aged Parsi gentleman approached me. He was a well known Karachi businessman, activist and columnist whose name I am withholding. Over the course of several meetings he told me his incredible tale. How he as a young man along with several of his school chums insouciantly removed the Gandhi statue in the dead of the night armed with some basic tools and a lorry – all while Karachi seethed with fear and hatred. It was then ferried to his father’s home, initially meant as a temporary abode until a handover to Indian representative could be organised. Unfortunately, the then Indian High Commissioner to the Dominion of Pakistan could not assure a safe passage and refused. And that was how the Cowasjees became the involuntary guardians of Gandhi in PakistanThe Parsi gentleman was clear that his part in the story had to come to an end. We were now in the early 1980’s. General Zia’s Islamisation project was well underway. Sharia laws had been introduced into the legal system. Strict Islamic punishments were to be meted out for crimes like adultery, theft and drinking of alcohol. Educational curriculums were being rigorously overhauled to promote religious studies and conformity with orthodox Islamic principles. Dress codes, especially for women, were being enforced. The sari, once common amongst upper class Pakistani women, was fast disappearing. An ongoing media clampdown weeded out content deemed as un-Islamic.Though historically Parsis, unlike other minorities in Pakistan, have enjoyed a somewhat protected status and though Ardeshir was and continued to be a fearless and outspoken critic of the political establishment, he was no longer comfortable with his role as the statue’s custodian. He asked me if the long delayed handover of the statue could finally take place.I immediately agreed. I was determined that the statue, now a priceless historical artifact, should come home on my watch. There was, however, a tricky logistical issue to navigate. Constant surveillance by Pakistani intelligence was a fact of life. So how could we transport the statue without compromising the Cowasjees.After clearance from Delhi, we decided to replicate the original midnight run. A non-descript truck, organised by the Consulate, picked up a large wrapped item from the Cowasjee residence and quietly brought it to the Indian mission late one summer night.I personally inspected the precious cargo. Through all its travails, the statue had endured some damage. One hand was broken and the glasses were cracked, but otherwise Gandhiji stood tall. We arranged for some minor repairs, and after a few weeks, the statue took pride of place in the Chancery reception. Suddenly confronted with this majestic but serene statue, surprised Pakistani visitors were often curious about its origins, but we remained tightlipped.Eventually, once the statue was properly restored, we arranged for its transportation to the High Commission in Islamabad. In hindsight, that last trek from Karachi to Islamabad turned out to be as consequential as the original journey in 1948. In 1993, following the demolition of the Babri Masjid, furious mobs in Pakistan attacked over 30 Hindu temples and in Karachi ransacked both the Consulate and the Consul General’s residence in which I had once lived.Valuable art was vandalised, including a beautiful painting by B. Prabha.Post the 1993 attacks, the Indian consulate in Karachi closed down. It remains shut to this day. In Islamabad, however, the Gandhi statue still stands, an enduring testament to “freedom, truth and non-violence” true to its original plaque.
Article Summary: One of only two gandhi statutes in pakistan, bapuji stands tall at the lobby of the indian high commission in islamabad. The tale of how a pre-partition statue found its way to its eventual home is a fascinating saga reflecting the tumultuous history of our two countries.

Article Title: 'I was reciting Hanuman Chalisa': flydubai 'hero' Captain Smit Machchhar tells PM Modi about cockpit ordeal
Article Text:
PM said the entire country is praying for Captain Smit Machchhar.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday spoke via video call with flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who helped foil his co-pilot's alleged attempt to crash an Israel-bound flight, and praised his courage, presence of mind and composure.During the conversation, Smit told the Prime Minister that whenever he faces difficulty, he recites the Hanuman Chalisa. He said he was reciting it during the tense moments aboard the flydubai flight as well.Captain Smit became emotional during the call and said it was a very special moment for him to speak with PM Modi. Article Title: India’s great hunt for oil: Inside the ₹84,000-crore Samudra Manthan mission
Article Text:
India is pushing for increased exploration of offshore oil and gas resources in various basins.

India's offshore oil hunt

From PM Modi's 2025 announcement to

Samudra Manthan

Where Rs 84,084 crore will go

Mahanadi is the immediate deepwater test

Mahanadi and Andaman in focus

Andaman is the frontier hunt

Krishna-Godavari is pushing deeper

Cauvery adds another deepwater target

The western offshore areas are also part of the plan

From geological potential to actual production

From discovery to production

India is taking its search for oil and natural gas deeper into the sea.The focus is now spread across the Mahanadi basin off Odisha, the frontier waters of the Andaman-Nicobar region, and deeper sections of the Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery basins. The government's latest assessment puts the hydrocarbon potential of India's eastern and western offshore basins at more than 5,600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE), with water depths extending to 3,000 metres.Recent discoveries in the Cauvery, Mahanadi and Andaman basins have strengthened the case for expanding offshore exploration.The push comes as India remains heavily dependent on imported energy. India is the world's third-largest consumer of crude oil and has an annual crude oil import bill of nearly $144 billion, or about ₹13 lakh crore, according to the government.There is another problem. Existing oil and gas fields naturally decline by around 6 to 7 percent each year. New discoveries are therefore essential to sustain domestic production.The current push is the latest stage of a decade-long effort to reshape India's upstream oil and gas sector.The government introduced the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) in 2016 and launched the Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP). It also moved from Production Sharing Contracts to Revenue Sharing Contracts and expanded the National Data Repository.The government subsequently opened almost 99 percent of the offshore areas earlier classified as "No-Go" for exploration. This made more than one million square kilometres of India's Exclusive Economic Zone available for exploration.Prime Minister Narendra Modi gave the next phase a mission-mode identity in his Independence Day address on August 15, 2025.Calling the effort a modern-day "Samudra Manthan", PM Modi said India would work in mission mode to find oil and gas reserves beneath the sea. He also announced the National Deep Water Exploration Mission.On July 31, 2026, the Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan, the National Offshore Exploration Scheme. The central sector scheme, under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, has an outlay of ₹84,084 crore through financial year 2030-31.The scheme allocates ₹28,534 crore for offshore seismic data acquisition, processing and interpretation, and ₹43,200 crore for 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration wells.The government will support up to 50 percent of eligible drilling costs, subject to a ceiling of ₹675 crore per well. The scheme also provides ₹10,000 crore for common offshore infrastructure, ₹2,000 crore for oil and gas manufacturing and services zones, and ₹350 crore for monitoring and support activities.But the real test of Samudra Manthan lies beneath the numbers.It is about where India is drilling, what it has already found, and whether those discoveries can eventually become producing fields.The Mahanadi Offshore Basin off Odisha is one of the most important tests of India's deepwater strategy.On July 25, Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri marked the start of drilling of MN-DWN18-1-HD, the first appraisal well in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin.It is the first of four planned deepwater wells intended to systematically evaluate the basin, which the government considers one of India's most prospective offshore areas.An appraisal well is drilled to determine the quality and commercial potential of an existing hydrocarbon discovery. The four-well programme is therefore an important step beyond seismic interpretation. It is designed to establish how significant the basin's discoveries could actually be.Government records show that ONGC had already made two gas discoveries in the Mahanadi offshore area after the opening of the former No-Go zones. One of these was in a block where 94 percent of the area had earlier been classified as No-Go.But finding hydrocarbons is only the first step.The Mahanadi basin also highlights why Samudra Manthan includes a major infrastructure component. The government says several offshore discoveries remain undeveloped because production and evacuation costs are too high, particularly in the Mahanadi and Kutch basins.The scheme's ₹10,000 crore common infrastructure component is aimed at tackling that problem.Further east, the Andaman-Nicobar offshore basin represents a more frontier form of exploration.The government's 2017 Hydrocarbon Resource Assessment Study estimated hydrocarbon resources in the Andaman-Nicobar basin at 371 MMTOE. Following HELP, four blocks covering approximately 23,261 square kilometres were allocated for oil and gas exploration. Government data says exploration in those blocks generated 8,501 line kilometres of 2D seismic data, 3,270 square kilometres of 3D seismic data and three drilled wells.Another four blocks covering 47,058 square kilometres were subsequently offered in the Andaman basin under OALP-X.ONGC and Oil India have taken exploration into the ultra-deepwater region, with drilling operations targeting depths of up to 5,000 metres.One important well is ONGC's ANDW-7 in the East Andaman Back Arc region. The well encountered traces of light crude and condensate in cutting samples, C-5 neo-pentane in trip gases and reservoir-quality facies. The government said the findings provided evidence of an active thermogenic petroleum system in the region, comparable with petroleum systems in Myanmar and North Sumatra.The findings do not establish a commercially producing field. The government has said commercial reserves in the Andaman campaign remain to be established. Their significance lies in providing evidence of a working petroleum system that can guide further exploration.The Krishna-Godavari basin off India's eastern coast is a more established offshore hydrocarbon province but remains central to the country's deepwater strategy.In OALP Round VIII, the 2022 KG-UDWHP-2022/1 ultra-deepwater block in the Krishna-Godavari basin covered 1,199.64 square kilometres. This was the size of that particular block, not the total current exploration acreage of the basin.The Krishna-Godavari basin has also attracted international technical collaboration. In 2022, ONGC signed a Heads of Agreement with ExxonMobil for deepwater exploration covering the Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery basins on the eastern coast and the Kutch-Mumbai region on the western coast.The Cauvery Offshore Basin is another important part of India's eastern offshore exploration map.The government's 2026 Samudra Manthan backgrounder cites recent finds in the Cauvery, Mahanadi and Andaman basins as evidence supporting the broader offshore opportunity.The basin is part of India's wider effort to identify additional offshore resources through deeper and more technically demanding exploration.Samudra Manthan is not confined to India's eastern coast. The western offshore belt, including Kutch and Mumbai Offshore, is also part of the country's wider exploration strategy.The government has identified Mahanadi and Kutch as areas where common offshore infrastructure is particularly important because high production and evacuation costs can prevent discoveries from moving into production.OALP Round VIII in 2022 included blocks in Mumbai Offshore, Kutch, Saurashtra and Kerala-Konkan. ONGC's collaboration with ExxonMobil also covered the Kutch-Mumbai region, keeping the western offshore belt within India's broader deepwater exploration push.The numbers attached to Samudra Manthan describe a large opportunity, but they do not mean India already has 5,600 MMTOE of proven offshore reserves waiting to be produced.The government estimates more than 5,600 MMTOE of hydrocarbon potential across India's eastern and western offshore basins. Separately, subject to exploration success, Samudra Manthan aims to add more than 600 MMTOE of hydrocarbon reserves, expand the country's hydrocarbon resource base from 1.6 billion tonnes of oil equivalent to 2.2 billion tonnes of oil equivalent, and increase annual domestic oil and gas production from around 62 MMTOE to 80 MMTOE.The government says the additional production could eventually reduce crude oil imports by nearly ₹1 lakh crore a year.The distinction between potential, reserves and production is critical. Seismic surveys identify promising geological structures, but drilling is required to establish whether hydrocarbons are actually present. A discovery then needs appraisal, reserve estimation and commercial assessment before it can move into development and production.Samudra Manthan therefore goes beyond drilling. Its ₹84,084 crore framework combines geological data acquisition, deepwater drilling support, common infrastructure, and domestic manufacturing and services capacity.The immediate picture is spread across different stages. Mahanadi is in an appraisal campaign designed to evaluate hydrocarbon discoveries. Andaman remains a frontier basin where geological evidence points to an active petroleum system, but commercial reserves have yet to be established. Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery remain important eastern offshore targets for deeper exploration, while Kutch and other western offshore areas form part of the wider exploration and infrastructure strategy.Samudra Manthan is therefore not simply India's ₹84,084 crore plan to drill more wells. It is the latest stage of a decade-long effort to open offshore acreage, improve geological data, encourage exploration and build the infrastructure needed to bring commercially viable discoveries into production.The decisive test will be whether prospects beneath the Mahanadi, Andaman, Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery and other offshore areas can make the journey from geological potential to commercially recoverable reserves and, finally, to actual oil and gas production in India.
Article Summary: The focus is now spread across the mahanadi basin off odisha, the frontier waters of the andaman-nicobar region, and deeper sections of the krishna-godavari and cauvery basins. The government's latest assessment puts the hydrocarbon potential of india's eastern and western offshore basins at more than 5,600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent.

NEW DELHI: At a time when pilots’ mental health has emerged as a key concern post some recent events, with flydubai cockpit fight being the most recent one, India’s restrictive rules for cockpit crew to leaves domestic airlines only after serving long notice periods could be adding to their stress. The rule for a co-pilot to serve six months’ notice and a captain a year (which has been challenged legally), has made it difficult for foreign airlines to hire Indian aviators as they mostly want people to join in three months. Now with Captain Smit Machchhar proving his mettle in flydubai, the budget arm of Dubai’s mega carrier Emirates, Indian pilots hope foreign airlines — primarily in Gulf and other places like Sri Lanka and South Korea — keep the Indian reality in mind while giving them offer letters.“We usually don’t hire direct from India and prefer if a pilot has worked in a second country before onboarding them,” a senior official of a leading West Asian airline had recently told TOI. The reasons are two-fold: India’s notice period requirement, which remains binding for pilots even if the employer in India defaults on contractual obligations like paying on time, and then informal tie-ups with big Indian carriers against “poaching.A senior official of an airline here said: “Because of the notice period requirement, some pilots here give ‘fake resignation’ in advance and then look for jobs so that they can leave in three months of getting a job abroad. And if they don’t get a job, they take the fake resignation back.”The notice period rule has been challenged by pilots in court and the matter is sub judice. “There are concerns about pilots’ state of mind due to what could be going on in their personal lives. This notice period rule, meant to ensure schedule integrity of airlines by preventing sudden mass resignations, has outlived its utility. Today India has two big and well-funded airline and a few emerging ones. Now it is only protecting airlines that are unable to pay,” said a pilot.

Article Title: The average will never applaud the exceptional
Article Text:
The Final Problem’

“Venmai Enappaduvadhu Yaadhenin, Onmai

Udayam Yaam Ennum Serukku.”

“What is mediocrity? It is the vanity that declares, ‘I am wise.’”

A doctor by profession, Arthur Conan Doyle travelled to the Arctic, supported the early use of vaccines when they were still viewed with apprehension, and wrote poetry, drama, history and fiction. He was also an enthusiastic sportsman and introduced skiing in Switzerland’s Alps mountains.But none of these achievements would define his place in popular imagination as the creation of one character: Sherlock Holmes.Holmes became legendary because he was more than a detective. He observed what others overlooked, questioned what others accepted and followed reason where intuition might have led people astray. Doyle gave him a mind of extraordinary precision.There were interesting contradictions between the author and the character he created. Holmes does not believe in ghosts, but Doyle deeply believed in conversations with spirits!Some of the quotations by Holmes are intense and sets you to think. “There is nothing more deceptive than an obvious fact.” “When you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.” And, with characteristic arrogance, he declares, “I am my brain, the rest of me is merely an appendix.”Doyle eventually grew frustrated that Holmes had overshadowed everything else he had written. So, in ‘, published in 1893, he killed Holmes, sending him and his arch-rival Professor Moriarty plunging to their deaths at the Reichenbach Falls.The readers could not accept this.There was outrage and thousands of cancellations of magazine subscriptions. Doyle had underestimated the bond between Holmes and his readers. Eventually he resurrected him in another story.Among Holmes’s many quotations, one particularly catches my attention:“Mediocrity knows nothing higher than itself. But talent instantly recognises genius.”There is something profound in both halves of that sentence.Mediocrity is not necessarily a lack of talent, nor is something to be looked down upon. The danger lies elsewhere: when comfort becomes a reason not to acknowledge efforts of others. The word mediocrity has a Latin root that means – ‘halfway up the mountain’.Perhaps that is why the mediocre mind often struggles to acknowledge greatness. When someone spends years pursuing a mission; a writer writing, an artist creating, an entrepreneur building, a reformer changing, there may be someone who asks, “But he did not make any money” or “She did not take care of her family”. Lest they understand that the pursuit for greatness is fulfilling in itself.And that is where the second half of Holmes’s observation becomes even more powerful.‘Talent recognises genius’.Helen Keller, deaf and blind, met M S Subbulakshmi when she visited India in 1955. When MS began to sing, Keller gently placed her fingers on the singer’s throat, sensing the vibrations of the music. Deeply moved, she is remembered for telling MS, “You sing like an angel.”How beautifully one extraordinary person spotted another.Long before Holmes, Thiruvalluvar had captured the human weakness of mediocrity with astonishing precision. In Kural 844, he says:The mountain does not become smaller because someone has stopped climbing.And greatness may simply be the courage to keep looking upward.
Article Summary: Holmes became legendary because he was more than a detective. He observed what others overlooked, questioned what others accepted and followed reason where intuition might have led people astray. Doyle gave him a mind of extraordinary precision. Holmes does not believe in ghosts, but doyle deeply believed in conversations with spirits.

Five Indian nationals aboard a Kuwait-flagged crude oil tanker were safely rescued after the vessel was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, the Indian embassy in Oman said on Friday.The Indian nationals were aboard MT Kazimah III, which was hit while sailing through the strategic waterway. The embassy coordinated their rescue and said all five had been safely shifted ashore.“Earlier today, the Mission coordinated rescue of five Indian nationals on board the Kuwait-flagged tanker MT Kazimah III, struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. All 5 Indian nationals have been shifted ashore safely. We thank the Omani authorities for their continued support and assistance,” the embassy said in a post on X.The embassy thanked Omani authorities for their support during the rescue operation.MT Kazimah III is a crude oil tanker sailing under the Kuwaiti flag and was en route to the port of Lomé in Togo when it was struck.The incident comes as India steps up efforts to monitor the safety of its seafarers amid heightened security risks in the Persian Gulf and other major shipping routes.Earlier on Tuesday, external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that more than 4,500 Indian seafarers were aboard commercial vessels operating in the region. Of these, 163 were on 12 active cargo ships, including six India-flagged vessels and six foreign-flagged vessels carrying cargo to India.“At this point, we have six India-flagged commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf. We also have six foreign-flagged vessels which are carrying cargo to India. So 12 ships are there. On these ships, we have around 163 Indian seafarers who are on board,” Jaiswal said during a media briefing.“Apart from this, we also have over 4,500 Indian seafarers who are on board various commercial vessels which are operating in the area,” he added.Jaiswal said the ministry of shipping was coordinating with Indian diplomatic missions and local stakeholders to track vessel movements and monitor the welfare of Indian seafarers.“Our ministry of shipping continues to monitor the movement of these ships and is looking at the well-being of all these seafarers, and as and when required, through our embassies and other stakeholders, they do the needful for their well-being and welfare,” he stated.“On our side, we remain committed to the safety and well-being of our seafaring community abroad,” Jaiswal said.The incident comes amid growing risks to commercial shipping across the Persian Gulf, Red Sea and Black Sea, where vessels have faced repeated attacks.External affairs minister S Jaishankar had raised concerns over attacks on commercial vessels and seafarers during his address to the 81st United Nations general assembly last week.“New challenges in the maritime domain have added to longstanding ones on land. There have been attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Gulf and from the Red Sea to the Black Sea. Indian seafarers have lost their lives, as have others from other nations.This is completely unacceptable,” Jaishankar told the UN assembly.Jaishankar said India had joined Liberia and 23 partner nations in an international coalition aimed at mobilising global public opinion and defending commercial shipping routes.“We must ensure that the safety and security of shipping and seafarers is never compromised. Scrupulously observing international law is an integral element of that endeavour,” Jaishankar urged.He also called for immediate restraint and de-escalation in the Gulf to protect civilian crews and ensure the uninterrupted movement of energy supplies and global trade.

Bleeding on the cockpit floor after being attacked by his co-pilot, Captain Smit Machchhar said his thoughts were fixed on saving all 174 passengers as the assailant frenetically tried to crash the aircraft. Drawing strength from Hanuman Chalisa, he made a final push to open the cockpit door, allowing others to overpower the attacker and steer the plane to safety.In his first publicly available account, Machchhar spoke from his Abu Dhabi hospital bed to PM Narendra Modi by video call Friday. “I was fighting for my life, but I was determined not to let others die. There was a moment when I was lying down, when I realised that the plane was going down,” he said.Machchhar said he had told himself to get up and act. “I have been flying planes for 17 years, I have been a captain for the last 11 years, and I know what is happening in an aircraft even with my eyes closed... I was being attacked, but I made a last push and opened the door,” he said, praising those who rushed into the cockpit and seized the violent co-pilot.Raw emotions took over him for a while as Machchhar spoke to Modi about those dramatic moments and called him his idol.The PM responded that his courage had made Smit a global hero, with people worldwide offering prayers for his good health, and shown that Indians save lives rather than take them. “You have boosted the prestige of 140 crore Indians,” Modi said, adding: “You saved everyone. You’ve done a very great job. ”Modi also thanked govts of Saudi Arabia and UAE for caring for Machchhar. Referring to social media reactions, he said people wondered what India and its pilots might have suffered without Machchhar’s intervention. You have shown the world what the true meaning of ‘ahimsa’ is,” Modi said. He later posted the call online with the message: “An unforgettable conversation with Captain Smit, filled with pride and emotions.”Machchhar said the call lifted his morale: “Receiving a call from you makes me feel so proud. Now I feel proud of myself too. I did not have this feeling so far. I am sorry I am crying in front of you.”When Machchhar said he had never imagined speaking to Modi, the PM replied that his deed had made people worldwide eager to see and speak to him. Modi briefly spoke to him in Gujarati and said the country was eager to greet him after his recovery.Machchhar said work may keep him outside India but not away from its culture. NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Friday said Bharat’s identity was rooted in its diversity of languages, faiths, castes and cultures, and that the country could contribute to building a better world by combining its traditional knowledge with modern progress.Addressing a gathering at Prabhadevi in Mumbai, Bhagwat said the younger generation should be taught about Indian society and its traditions while also drawing on knowledge from across the world for the betterment of society.Bhagwat recalled an interaction at an interfaith meeting where a participant told him that religious conflicts were causing loss of human lives but that a solution to the problem was not readily available.“He asked me to come to his country and spread the teachings and knowledge of Bharat to the world,” Bhagwat said.The RSS chief said the eternal knowledge contained in the Bhagavad Gita was reflected in various traditions in India and elsewhere, although the expressions and words differed depending on the time and circumstances.“The conclusion of various philosophies, from ancient traditions to the latest one, is the same.From the ancient period of human beings who wondered about the world till Yuval Noah Harari (Israeli medievalist and historian), the range of thoughts and their conclusions are the same,” he said.People need to understand eternal truth to understand the world, their surroundings and how they should conduct themselves, Bhagwat said.He added that different traditions may use different expressions to communicate the same fundamental principles and that people should focus on the direction of those teachings rather than merely their outward expressions.“If you ignore the message and only focus on the choice of words, it creates confusion,” he said.Bhagwat also referred to scientific studies on consciousness and said, “Today, the world has one common consciousness. It is the beginning of everything. Everything started by a pre-existing universal consciousness.”He compared the intellect to a driver, the soul to the owner and the different parts of the body to the horses of a chariot. Ego, he said, could sometimes misdirect a person and lead to sorrow and disappointment, making guidance important when dealing with challenges in life.“With a minor disappointment, people get frustrated and some even end their lives. If you want to do daily things, you need guidance. Those who have lived life like that have told us,” he said.Bhagwat said great personalities and their works provided guidance to society, helping people preserve their values while adapting to changing circumstances.Speaking about the youth, he said members of Gen Z who go abroad are often reminded that their origins lie in Bharat, its traditions and knowledge. People want them to explain the country’s specialities and identity, he added.Bhagwat recalled an example shared by a participant who described Bharat as an impressive country after visiting a state-of-the-art oil refinery in Jamnagar, Gujarat.Amid the activity at the refinery, the participant noticed a huge idol of Lord Ganesha and remarked, “That is Bharat”, Bhagwat said.“This is the identity of Bharat and we have a sense of pride in it. It should be passed on to the next generation,” he said.The RSS chief said the younger generation should be taught how to face upcoming challenges, continue moving forward regardless of success or failure and make their lives meaningful.Bhagwat also noted that it was often said that members of the new generation did not have a strong command over their mother tongue and that the attention span of the current generation was also shorter.
Article Summary: Rashtriya swayamsevak sangh (rss) mohan bhagwat addresses a gathering in mumbai. He said bharat’s identity was rooted in its diversity of languages, faiths, castes and cultures. He added that the country could contribute to building a better world by combining traditional knowledge with modern progress.

Article Title: 'Their time is up': Akhilesh Yadav slams Centre over police action at Jantar Mantar protest against CEC
Article Text:
Opposition leaders and activists were detained at Jantar Mantar during a protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the SIR exercise

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday criticised the Centre over the detention of opposition leaders and activists during protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise at Jantar Mantar.“When a government becomes weak, it resorts to injustice. When the time comes for a government to leave office, it files false cases and puts pressure on people,” Yadav said.“Those who have been winning elections through the Election Commission have faced allegations from time to time. People across the country and all political parties are raising questions about the credibility of the Election Commission and the government. At such a time, the government and constitutional institutions should at least remain impartial. They compromise their impartiality because they appear weak. Their time is up, and that is why they are resorting to injustice and sending people to jail,” he added.RJD leader Manoj Jha, CPM leader Brinda Karat, CPI national secretary P Sandosh Kumar, CPI Delhi secretary Prof Dinesh Varshney, AISF general secretary Dinesh Seerangara, and social activists Yogendra Yadav and Nikhil Dey were among those detained.Delhi Police detained more than 700 people, including AAP leaders like Atishi and members of several student organisations like Neha Bora, at Jantar Mantar and surrounding areas, according to police. The protest site and roads leading to it were heavily barricaded.Police maintained that no permission had been granted for the protest in the area, which remains under restrictions.'Vote chor, gaddi chhod'Jha, who was taken to the Badarpur Border area, criticised the police action on Gandhi Jayanti.“Today is Gandhi Jayanti... It is shameful that they are behaving like this...” news agency PTI quoted Jha saying as he was taken inside a bus.“This is all 'Godse-vadi' people can do on Gandhi Jayanti. They don't understand the essence of Gandhi,” he said earlier.Brinda Karat said, “Godse was Gandhi's murderer. People of Godse's ideology are in power in the Centre. Today they are murdering democracy through vote theft,” and called for Kumar's resignation.Social activist Nikhil Dey said, “We had requested permission for a peaceful protest on Gandhi Jayanti. This is a blot on a nation that was born out of 'satyagraha'... The only place in Delhi for peaceful protest, Jantar Mantar, is being taken away on Gandhi Jayanti… Section 163 cannot be a law in free Indian democracy.”Protesters raised slogans including “vote chor gaddi chhod” demanding Kumar's removal. A group also raised, “ek kachori do samosa, Gyanesh tera kya bharosa.”The CPI said hundreds of its, AISF and AIYF cadres were detained and accused the government of using police force to suppress the protest.

Police detained more than 700 people, including aap leaders like atishi and members of several student organisations.

Article Title: 'Exceptional courage': Pilots body writes to PM Modi, requests bravery award for Smit Machchhar
Article Text:
Pilots’ body seeks national recognition for Captain Smit Machchhar

NEW DELHI: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday seeking an appropriate national bravery award for flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, citing his “exceptional courage” and professional conduct during the mid-air emergency on September 30.The pilots' body said Machchhar, the pilot-in-command of flydubai flight FZ1073, was reportedly attacked by the first officer with a crash axe and sustained serious injuries during the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight.Despite being injured, Machchhar continued to discharge his responsibilities as pilot-in-command, maintained control of the aircraft and ultimately diverted it safely to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, FIP said."The Federation of Indian Pilots respectfully submits that acts of exceptional courage such as this deserve recognition at the highest appropriate level. We therefore request the Hon'ble Prime Minister's Office to kindly consider Capt. Smit for an appropriate National Bravery Award / national civilian recognition, in accordance with the applicable Government of India provisions and after due verification of the facts by the competent authorities," it said in a letter."Capt. Smit's actions demonstrate that, even when confronted with grave personal danger and serious injury, the responsibility of a true professional pilot remains firmly centred on the safety of those entrusted to his care," the pilots body said.The organisation noted that 174 passengers and eight crew members were onboard the flight and said Machchhar's actions under extreme personal danger contributed to bringing the aircraft safely to an alternate airport.FIP's appeal comes after Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora also wrote to PM Modi, urging the government to consider Machchhar for the Ashoka Chakra. Deora said the Mumbai-born pilot's actions demonstrated “courage, selflessness and duty” in an extreme situation.ALSO READ: 'Terrorist act': UAE official on flydubai attack, praises India pilot Smit Machchhar Machchhar was allegedly attacked by his co-pilot during the flight, following which passengers and other crew members intervened. The aircraft had transmitted emergency signals and rapidly lost altitude before being diverted to Saudi Arabia.The UAE has ordered an investigation into the incident, including the circumstances, motives and any possible links to terrorist activity or prior planning.PM Modi has also spoken to Machchhar over a video call and praised his courage, presence of mind and composure during the incident.
Article Summary: Pilots’ body seeks national recognition for captain smit machchhar for his 'exceptional courage' the federation of indian pilots (fip) wrote to prime minister narendra modi on friday seeking an appropriate national bravery award for flydubai pilot.
